tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: The variation of density of a solid cylindrical rod of cross sectional area $\alpha$ and length $L$ is $\rho=\rho_0 \frac{x^2}{L^2}$, where x is the distance from one end of the rod. The position of its centre of mass from one end $(x=0)$ is

solution.text: $\rho=\rho_0 \frac{x^2}{L^2}$, $\begin{aligned} & X=\frac{\int x d m}{\int d m} \quad d m=\alpha d x \rho=\frac{\alpha \rho_0 x^2}{L^2} d x \\ & =\frac{\rho_0 \int_0^L x^3 d x}{\frac{\rho_0}{L^2} \int_0^L x^2 d x}=\frac{\left[x^4 / 4\right]_0^L}{\left[x^3 / 3\right]_0^L}=3 / 4 L\end{aligned}$
